title: Simulateur: a stock-market game with a live market

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Picture a classroom of teams, all trading fictional stocks while prices flicker in real time. That's Simulateur.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A stock-market game. Who sets it up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: An admin. In a five-step dashboard they define the settings, create fictional companies and stocks, build teams, add news and events, and review the scenario. It's built with Django for AlgoÉTS, for groups who want to play a market game together.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And how do prices move if the companies aren't real?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A price engine generates a new candle for every stock at each time step, using a chosen noise model like Brownian motion, Perlin noise or Monte Carlo. Each candle is saved and pushed to the players over a live WebSocket connection.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Join a team with a link, buy and sell at the latest price, follow their holdings and watch leaderboards. The admin can even have a local Ollama language model draft news, events or whole scenarios.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's also a backtesting app on the side. And a single run script installs everything and starts the demo.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The full write-up explains the price models in detail.
